latest.title: Ceres spins out RFC Power
latest.content:

Ceres Power Holdings plc

CWR.L
26 August 2026
Ceres Power Holdings plc
("Ceres", the "Company")
Ceres spins out RFC Power
Horsham, UK:
Ceres Power Holdings plc (CWR.L), a leading developer of clean energy technology, today
provides an update on its ownership position in RFC Power Ltd.
RFC Power is a manganese flow battery technology company specialising in long-duration energy storage and, in September 2025, became a fully owned subsidiary within the Ceres Group following the acquisition of its remaining share capital and intellectual property for a nominal amount.
RFC Power today announced a £10 million Series A funding round, led by the British Business Bank, with participation from Centrica plc, Ceres and Temasek Trust's Catalytic Capital for Climate and Health ("C3H"). The cash contribution from Ceres amounts to £1 million, with an additional £1.5 million of equity to be issued to Ceres in exchange for in-kind engineering services. RFC Power has a post money value of c.£12 million.
Following the fundraise, Ceres will retain c.37% ownership of RFC Power and will receive a share of future revenues from all products sold. Ceres' Chief Financial Officer Stuart Paynter will also join the Board of RFC Power. Following completion of the fundraise and change in ownership, RFC Power has been rebranded to Certain Energy.
Stuart Paynter, Chief Financial Officer of Ceres commented,
"Ceres sees potential in Certain Energy's low‑cost flow‑battery technology, its role in long‑duration energy storage, and its alignment with Ceres' existing solid oxide technology. We are excited to see Certain Energy enter this next phase of growth and we remain a supportive shareholder."

Ceres Power Holdings plc

Doosan Fuel Cell SOFC order with Reverion GmbH
Horsham, UK:
Ceres Power Holdings plc (CWR.L), a leading developer of clean energy technology, notes the contract between Doosan Fuel Cell and Reverion GmbH for the supply SOFC stacks under license from Ceres, worth approximately 108.7 billion KRW (c£60 million), to be supplied to overseas power facilities in Germany and Europe. This is Doosan's first contract to export SOFC technology overseas.
For more information, please see the article here:
Doosan Fuel Cell exports SOFC core components overseas for the first time - Business Plus
About Reverion
Reverion
produces reversible fuel cell power systems that make gas to power and power to gas applications truly efficient. Its patented system can generate electricity, methane or hydrogen with up to 80% electrical efficiency while integrating energy storage and carbon capture. Reverion supplies their reversible power plants to applications across the biogas industry, utilities, sector coupling, data centres and long-duration energy storage.
About Doosan Fuel Cell
Doosan Fuel Cell is a subsidiary of Doosan Group, which has a history of over 129 years, making it the oldest conglomerate in South Korea. As a leading fuel cell solution provider with proprietary technology for the world's first commercial fuel cell, Doosan Fuel Cell offers hydrogen solutions including PAFC (Phosphoric Acid Fuel Cell) and SOFC (Solid Oxide Fuel Cell). They provide integrated solutions encompassing the design, technology development, manufacturing, installation, operation, and maintenance of key fuel cell technologies such as stacks and systems. Doosan Fuel Cell, which established the world's first and largest hydrogen fuel cell power plant, is expanding its business area beyond stationary power to include mobility through marine models. The company is committed to addressing climate change and achieving Net-Zero. For more details, please visit its website at www.doosanfuelcell.com or follow it on LinkedIn.

company_30s.what_they_do: Ceres Power designs and sells polymer‑electrolyte membrane fuel cells that turn hydrogen into electricity. Their products power heavy‑duty vehicles, backup power systems and other stationary loads.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Hydrogen fuel cells are a key technology for zero‑emission transport and grid decarbonisation. Ceres Power sits at the front of a growing market that is backed by governments, automotive OEMs and infrastructure providers worldwide.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is still working to scale production and secure large orders. It has recently spun off a subsidiary, raised fresh capital, and secured a new contract with Doosan. The company is still operating at a loss but is moving from a cash‑burn phase to a more focused growth stage.

rns_narrative: The company is restructuring: a spin‑out of RFC Power, a vote‑rights change and a capital raise that give it a cleaner balance sheet and a clearer product focus.
It has just landed a Doosan fuel‑cell order and released interim results that show improved cash flow, signalling that the business model is starting to work.
A retail book offer indicates the market is slowly warming to the stock and that price discovery is beginning to take shape.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Skeptical optimism – the crowd is quietly watching the new order while still wary of profitability.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls point to the Doosan deal as proof of demand and to the spin‑out as a move that will sharpen the company’s focus. They see a potential turnaround if the new product line scales.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears argue the company has yet to hit earnings and still relies on external financing. They fear the hydrogen market may slow and that the firm could be left with excess capacity.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Sentiment has shifted from negative to neutral. The Doosan announcement lifted chatter, but the overall tone remains cautious because the company has not yet turned a profit.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – the market is silent, which gives a contrarian trader the best chance for a surprise bounce.

near_term_catalysts: Full delivery of the Doosan order – a clear revenue event that will validate the product.
Q4 earnings that show a meaningful improvement in cash burn or a positive margin trend.
Any partnership announcement that expands the commercial fleet customer base.
A spike in volume that breaks the 20‑day moving average, indicating institutional buying.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for the share price to break above the 20‑day moving average with at least 30% higher volume, and for the company to publish a revised guidance that lifts the target price. A sudden drop in the 52‑week high would be a warning sign.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stage of a deep crash‑recovery cycle. A clear bottom has likely been reached, but the price still sits far below the 52‑week low. A sustained bounce from the current trough would confirm mean‑reversion.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the share climbs to a level 40% below its pre‑crash peak, that is a 100% upside – a classic 2‑to‑1 reward. The recent Doosan order and capital raise are the catalysts that can bring the price back to that midpoint. The deep crash (≈80% fall) means the risk is capped at the remaining 20% of the pre‑crash value, giving a clear asymmetry.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The firm still has no earnings and a high burn rate. If the hydrogen market stalls or the Doosan order is delayed, the price could fall another 10–20% before stabilising. The worst case is a further slide to the current trough, leaving the upside unrealised.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss: 20% of the pre‑crash price (≈25% of the current price). Potential gain: 100% of the pre‑crash price (≈200% of the current price). The asymmetry is roughly 1:4 – risk is small, reward is large.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the price closes above the 20‑day moving average with volume 30% higher than the 20‑day average. Size the position so that a 5% move against you would wipe out 1–2% of the account. Place a stop 5% below the entry to limit downside to the remaining 20% of the pre‑crash level.
playbook.if_watching: Hold until you see a clear volume spike coinciding with a price break above the 20‑day average or a positive earnings revision. If either occurs, consider a small entry to test the move.
playbook.if_passing: If the company announces bankruptcy, delisting, or a major fraud claim, exit immediately.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Ceres Power sits at the bottom of an 80% crash, has just secured a key Doosan contract and raised fresh capital – a classic contrarian set‑up with a 2‑to‑1 upside if the price rebounds to the midpoint of its pre‑crash range.
